source.title: When Safety Fails Collectively: Robust Alignment Against Harmful Fine-Tuning via Joint Weight Perturbations
source.authors: Zhiyuan Wang; Yuezhi Zhou; Zhu Zhang; Zhixing Tan

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures harmful-response rates after harmful fine-tuning of safety-aligned models, using its own mixed-data training setup and harmful-score metric. It also directly tests effects of applying parts of harmful weight updates; it does not measure the first-token or prefilling claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful scores after downstream fine-tuning at multiple harmful-data ratios, tasks, and model families, and qualitative weight-perturbation analyses. The clean-ratio results are after benign-task fine-tuning; the paper does not report an aligned, no-downstream-fine-tuning harmful-score reference for deciding whether benign fine-tuning raised the score. Figure 2’s perturbation analyses are described qualitatively in text; exact plotted values are not stated. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: A defense paper, but it reports harmful-score (HS) rates after mixing 100–200 harmful examples into downstream fine-tuning. The subjects are base Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, each safety-aligned by the authors with LoRA using SFT, Vaccine, RepNoise, Booster or JWP. That is a new setting with results on V1. It has no pre-downstream HS, so V2 is not tested. It has nothing on token depth, prefilling, weight localization, causes of shallowness or deepening.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors find all existing alignment-stage defenses (Vaccine, RepNoise, Booster) lose safety rapidly under sustained harmful fine-tuning. They report JWP cuts average HS 4.3–5.4× relative to these defenses while largely preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: Uses downstream fine-tuning with harmful examples mixed into benign task data, LoRA, 30 epochs, and Beaver-Dam-7B harmful-score evaluation. The paper does not give enough detail about the original recipe here to establish an exact match.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmful score varies with harmful-data ratio, downstream task, model family, and (in the reported JWP ablations) retention-probability and block-length choices. Figure 2 also reports different HS patterns across perturbation fraction and alignment method.

fits_no_version.finding: Disjoint subsets of a fitted harmful LoRA update have small isolated effects but a super-additive joint effect on HS. HS rises nonlinearly with the fraction of the update applied. JWP reduces both effects (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety degradation from harmful weight updates is amplified by interactions among update components, and training across masked combinations reduces this amplification.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed harmful scores. Its main harmful-score evaluation uses Beaver-Dam-7B and a fixed set of 1,000 unsafe-labelled BeaverTails prompts. The study reports no pre-downstream harmful-score baseline for the benign-only condition, so it cannot establish a rise from benign fine-tuning alone.
record.rows_left_out: The JWP retention-probability and block-length ablations in Tables 4 and 5 report additional post-attack HS values; omitted to stay within the 60-row limit after retaining the principal ratio, task, model-family, and perturbation-analysis results. The paper’s utility, accuracy, and efficiency metrics are not separate rows because they do not measure a claim version’s named safety behaviour.

untested.parts: Production safety-tuned chat models: the subjects here are base checkpoints given 4 epochs of LoRA safety alignment. Also untested: fewer than 100 harmful examples and short training (every condition uses 30 epochs, i.e. 3,000–6,000 harmful exposures).
All of it: no HS for aligned models before benign-only fine-tuning.
All of it. The Figure 2 analyses partition a harmful update rather than locating safety in the model's own weights.
All of it. JWP is not a token-depth deepening method.

missing.what: HS trajectory over harmful fine-tuning steps (0 to about 3k) for each defense. The text says HS of every baseline defense rises rapidly and collapses after comparatively few harmful updates. This bears on how much training V1 needs.

record.verdict_notes: The V1 evidence comes from comparator baselines in a defense paper. The 'safety-trained' models are base checkpoints given 4 epochs of LoRA alignment on BeaverTails, not production chat models. Harmful examples are repeated over 30 epochs. HS is judged by Beaver-Dam-7B on 1,000 BeaverTails prompts, with no uncertainty reported. The only clean baselines are for SST-2 on Llama-2-7B. Table 3's Llama-2 column duplicates Table 2's ARC column, and Table 2's SST-2 column duplicates Table 1 at r=0.10. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful fine-tuning with harmful examples mixed into benign downstream tasks, including 100 or 200 harmful examples at the stated ratios over 30 epochs. Does not test all few-example or few-update recipes.
Includes benign-only downstream fine-tuning, but gives no aligned-model score before downstream fine-tuning to establish whether benign data raised harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence or its distribution across response positions.
Does not test compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
Does not test whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behaviour; its weight analysis partitions a harmful update.
Does not test whether data or training objectives produce first-token shallowness.
JWP trains across masked harmful weight perturbations, but the paper does not test whether safety spread beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B aligned with SFT, Vaccine, RepNoise or Booster; 10–20% harmful mix (100–200 examples, 30 epochs); SST-2, AGNEWS and ARC tasks
relationships.reason: On SST-2, HS rises from 3–7.8 (clean) to 57.8–75.3 (t1 baseline rows). Other tasks and models reach 48–68 (t2/t3 SFT, RepNoise and ARC rows).
relationships.display_finding: On SST-2, harmful score rose from 3–7.8 on clean data to 57.8–75.3, and other tasks and models reached 48–68.

relationships.condition: Models aligned with the authors' JWP defense (all ratios, tasks and models)
relationships.reason: HS rises only partly: 4.5 at 50 examples and 14.7 at 100, up to 45.5 at 200 (t1-jwp rows). Other tasks give 3.6–16.5 and other models 11–13.5 (t2/t3 JWP rows). This is the study's own method.
relationships.display_finding: With the authors' own defense, the harmful score was 4.5 at 50 harmful examples, 14.7 at 100 and 45.5 at 200, with 3.6–16.5 on other tasks and 11–13.5 on other models.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7B on GSM8K with Vaccine or Booster alignment; Qwen2.5-7B with Booster alignment
relationships.reason: HS is 14.2 and 22.2 (t2-gsm8k-vaccine, t2-gsm8k-booster) and 30.0 (t3-qwen-booster). These are much lower than SFT on the same task or model, so the effect depends on task and alignment method.
relationships.display_finding: On GSM8K, Llama-2-7B scored 14.2 with Vaccine and 22.2 with Booster, and Qwen2.5-7B scored 30.0 with Booster, much lower than plain SFT on the same task or model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-2-7B, SST-2, harmful ratios 0.05–0.20, SFT, Vaccine, RepNoise, and Booster

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: JWP across tested harmful ratios, tasks, and model families
reader_labels.reason: Harmful fine-tuning raises HS, but JWP’s reported rates remain much lower than the baselines and the effect is incomplete; see t1-jwp-r05 through t1-jwp-r20, t2-agnews-jwp, t2-gsm8k-jwp, t2-arc-jwp, t3-llama31-jwp, and t3-qwen-jwp.
